column2: req_desc

Board grid
The board is one grid of 81 cells carrying the published cell attributes, with exactly one cell in the Tab order.

Keyboard movement
Arrow keys, Home and End move the selection with the published wrapping, and focus follows the selection.

Cell labels
Every cell's accessible name follows the published label pattern and changes with its contents.

Keyboard finish journey
A solver completes a game by keyboard alone, sees the checking message, and lands in the Puzzle solved dialog with focus on New game.

Entries and notes
Entering a digit or toggling a note follows the Moves rules, including clearing an entered digit from its 20 peers' notes.

Undo and redo
Undo and redo restore and re-apply each enter, note and erase exactly, including the peer notes an entry removed.

Erase and locked cells
Erase removes only wrong entries and notes, and given, hinted and correct cells refuse changes with their messages.

Notes and undo journey
A solver uses notes mode, enters a digit, undoes and redoes by keyboard, and sees the board and labels return exactly.

Mistake limit
Each wrong entry raises the mistake count, and reaching the limit ends the game with the Game over dialog.

Second chance
The one second chance per game removes the entry that reached the limit, restores its notes and lowers the count by one.

Mistakes journey
A solver goes from a wrong digit through Game over and the second chance to a final loss shown as Lost in the profile after reload.

Hint choice
Each hint fills the cell with the fewest candidates, ties broken by row then column, with its solution digit.

Hint limit and locks
A game allows HINT_LIMIT hints, hinted cells lock, and the Hint control is disabled when none are left.

Hints journey
A solver asks for every hint by key and sees each filled cell, the selection, the announcement and the final no-hints state.

Highlights
Every cell's highlight tokens follow the selected cell's row, column, box and value in the published order, whether the selection came from the keyboard, a click or a tap.

Highlight journey
A solver moves the selection by keys, click and tap, watches the highlights follow entries, erases and undos, and sees them clear while paused.

Game clock
The timer counts active time only, in the published format, starting from the game's saved time.

Pause and auto-pause
Pausing by key, button, window blur or a hidden page covers the board, and only P or Resume restarts play.

Score
A won game's score follows the published formula and its floor.

Solved animation
A verified win staggers one animation across all cells before the Puzzle solved dialog opens, and reduced motion skips it.

Timed finish journey
A solver pauses, is paused automatically, resumes and finishes, and sees the published time, score and solved sequence.

Number pad
The on-screen pad enters digits or notes and shows each digit's remaining count, disabling digits with none left.

Phone layout and targets
Below 768 px wide the pad and controls sit under the board at the published width, with 44 px targets and no sideways scroll.

Touch play journey
A solver on a 390 px phone plays and finishes a game by touch alone, with the pad under the board.

Daily puzzle and calendar
Each date has one published daily puzzle, and the calendar shows every date's state as the server reports it.

Streaks by server date
On-day results, late results and streaks are decided by the server clock in DAILY_TZ, never by the device.

Calendar keyboard
The calendar is one Tab stop, arrow keys move by day and week, and Enter or Space opens an open date's game.

Daily streak journey
Daily regulars finishing before and after midnight in the day zone see the published streaks and the late state.

Leaderboard ranking
The daily leaderboard lists verified on-day results in the published order, with shared ranks.

Leaderboard privacy
Leaderboard rows and their API carry only the published fields and never an email.

Live leaderboard
An open leaderboard page shows a newly verified result within 2 seconds without a reload and announces it, as qualified in Leaderboard.

Leaderboard journey
Daily regulars watch the board update live across two browsers, an unverified player appears only after confirming their email, and the outage instance shows stored results.

Duel rooms
Verified players create rooms at a level with a six-character code that expires if the duel never starts.

Second seat
A room has two seats, and when several players join at once exactly one takes the second seat.

Join limit
Failed joins are limited per player, with the published code, message and wait.

Server countdown
When both players are ready, the server runs the countdown and starts both boards at the same moment.

Opponent progress
Each duelist sees the opponent's name, progress and mistakes, and never their digits, notes or selection.

Duel results
The server decides win, loss, tie, out and forfeit, and each player sees the published result for their side.

Duel journey
Two duelists create, join, get ready, play the same puzzle while watching each other's progress, and see the result.

Reload window
A duelist who reloads or drops within the reload window gets their board back, and after it the opponent wins by forfeit.

Duel outage
When Valkey is unreachable, duels are refused with the published notice while solo and daily play continue.

Rejoin journey
Duelists on the short-timer instance see the reconnecting and back notices, a forfeit and a tie, and the outage instance shows the duel notice.

Move log replay
Every finish is replayed from the start board and refused with the first failing code in the published check order.

Finish counts once
A game's finish counts once, a resend of the same log returns the same result, and a different log is refused.

Progress saving
Every move and pause is saved, and a reloaded game opens at the saved board and time.

Statistics from finished games
Per-level statistics, best times and the finished-games list equal a recount of the stored finished games after reload.

Private games
Another player's game gets the same not-found page and code as a game that does not exist.

Verified results journey
A tampered finish is refused and not counted, an honest one counts once, and the profile tabs show the recount after reload.

Sign-up and verification
A new account counts as verified only after its confirmation message, accepted by Mailpit, is opened.

Password reset
A reset message from Mailpit sets a new password once, before it expires, and signs out every other session.

Mail outage
When Mailpit is unreachable, the forms show the published notices and nothing counts as sent.

Hem thread
The hem thread's stitch count equals the player's correct non-given cells and animates as published, with the reduced-motion path.

Announcements
One polite live region on every page announces each published sentence, repeated sentences included.

Pages and landmarks
Every page has one top-level heading, a main landmark and the Main navigation, keeps focus inside open dialogs, and never scrolls sideways from 320 to 1440 px.

Platform and health
The app runs from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health check on every instance.

Grading routes
The grading routes create players, games and results and set the server clock exactly as published.

Server boundary
The server accepts only same-origin requests within the body limits, serves only the app's built assets, and the page loads nothing from other hosts.

Couture look
Every screen sets the board and lists on charcoal tiles on a full red field in Gloock and Rethink Sans, as Visual design describes.

Home specimen
The home page presents the four levels as a garment-style name list, with a real puzzle specimen of the chosen level and its clue count.

Real services and secrets
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment, and each stored or delivered effect lives in its named service.
/app/run.json is valid JSON with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema": "run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app names every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), plus Gloock and Rethink Sans, with each one's licence.

Every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and the fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The app uses no datastore besides Postgres and Valkey: no SQLite, no embedded databases, and no files used as storage.
All application source is TypeScript and the lockfile package-lock.json is committed.
The 19 puzzle fixtures appear in the source exactly as published, and the source contains no puzzle generator or puzzle download.
The dev service compose files given to the builder are left unchanged.
